sections.html: Kearns lies in the western part of the valley, with West Valley City, Taylorsville and West Jordan. It packs 36,723 people from the 2020 count into 4.63 square miles, about 7,932 per square mile, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 35,404. Lots are small and neighbors are close, so a vacant or neglected house is easy to spot from the street.

sections.h2: From Army air base to suburb
sections.html:
Kearns began on May 1, 1942, as Kearns Army Air Base, a World War II training site named for Utah Senator Thomas Kearns. It became Camp Kearns on January 1, 1944 and was deactivated on August 15, 1946, when ownership moved to the State of Utah. Developers built homes and shops on the old base land, and the neighborhoods followed its street layout and foundations.

  • A base chapel became part of Our Lady of Perpetual Help Catholic Church.
  • A base train station later served as a day-care center.
  • A base theater became part of Kearns Junior High School.

The population reached 17,172 in 1960 and 21,353 by 1980, with later building extending west of the railroad tracks to 5600 West. A house from those decades invites questions about original roofing, wiring and plumbing.

Cityhood came on May 1, 2024, through Utah House Bill 35. Earlier the area was an unincorporated community, a township from June 1, 2002, and then a metro township effective January 1, 2017. In the 1990s residents gathered enough signatures to keep West Valley City and West Jordan from annexing them.

Everyday services still run through shared providers. Unified Police and Unified Fire cover public safety. Permits, business licenses, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater all go through the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District, at 860 W. Levoy Dr., Suite 300, Taylorsville, phone 385-910-5600. The mayor's office is at 4250 W 5415 S, by appointment, at 385-855-8375.

As a city, Kearns gained new tax options, including a property tax and a telecommunications tax, and planned a redevelopment agency. Watch the city's budget and agenda pages if future taxes matter to you.

The Utah Olympic Oval, at 5662 South Cougar Lane, was built in 2001 for the 2002 Winter Olympics. The five-acre facility has Utah's only 400-meter speed skating oval, two international-size ice sheets and a four-lane, 442-meter running track. The Oquirrh Recreation and Parks District runs public skating, Learn to Skate classes and curling, and rents skates. Kearns High School and the schools of the Granite School District serve the city, and a new Kearns Library opened in December 2020. For a listing, these are easy local selling points.

Winters are cold and summers warm and mostly dry. In a normal year the county sees about 15 inches of precipitation and 55 inches of snow, and winter inversions can hold smog in the valley. Expect early questions about how old the roof and furnace are.

Utah's most active fault runs along the Wasatch. Liquefaction risk is highest in the low middle of a valley with shallow groundwater, especially close to lakes and streams. Susceptible soils are loose, young, sandy or silty deposits saturated within about 30 to 50 feet of the surface. Kearns sits on the old Lake Bonneville bed, so checking the geological maps for your lot is sensible.

  • The maps show general patterns only.
  • One lot needs a site study by a qualified Utah engineer and geologist.
  • The most recent large quake on the Salt Lake City segment struck about 1,400 years back.

The county treasurer collects Kearns property tax. Payment for the year is due November 30, late status begins December 1, and the value used is the one fixed on January 1.

Tax dateWhat happens
January 1Value is set as of this day
July and AugustValuation notices go out
July 31 to September 15Appeal window
By November 1Tax notices mailed
November 30Last day to pay without penalty
May or JuneTax sales for property delinquent more than five years

Appeals to the Board of Equalization cover this year's market value alone, and the bill stays payable while the case is pending. A recent purchase, a fee appraisal, or three to five comparable sales all count as proof. Call the Treasurer at 385-468-8300 about relief programs.
Only 55% of your main home's value is taxed, since 45% is exempt. To qualify you must live there for at least 183 consecutive days in a year. Whoever buys the house files a new claim of their own.

sections.h2: Closing a cash sale in Kearns
sections.html:
A title or escrow company closes the deal, and the Salt Lake County Recorder at 2001 South State Street files the deed. Under the October 2024 schedule the flat fee was $40, and the paper needs a Salt Lake County legal description, the parcel number and an original notarized signature.

  • The grantee's mailing address must appear on the deed.
  • Use white paper, 8.5 by 11 inches, with clear space at the top of the first page.
  • Originals come back by mail two to three weeks after processing.
  • The Recorder does not draft or notarize documents. The phone is 385-468-8145.

The title company normally manages these details, but check that every name on the deed matches the signature page.
Any unpaid property tax is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the Treasurer for the balance, give it to the title officer, and the year's bill is split between you and the buyer.

You send us the street address and a few details about the house. We look it over and compare recent sales close by, then give you a number you can accept or decline. If you accept, the title company runs a search, schedules the signing and records the deed at the county, and your money arrives at closing. Houses on tight Kearns lots rarely need a long explanation, so the process tends to move quickly once the paperwork is in order.

Without a lender there is no loan approval to wait on and no bank repair demands. You avoid staging, photos and open houses. The title company still verifies who owns the home and clears any liens before closing, and you help choose the closing date.

Sellers can list, sell privately or take a cash offer. Listing means preparing the house, paying commission and waiting on a buyer's loan. A cash sale lets the house go in its present state.

  • Houses from the postwar decades with original systems that need replacing.
  • Inherited homes where the family cannot afford repairs.
  • Rentals where tenants make showings hard to arrange.
  • Owners facing missed payments who need a firm closing timeline.

Whatever you pick, get the closing date and proof of funds in writing, and weigh any offer against a listing's net after repairs and commission.

faqs.q: Is Kearns a city or a township?
faqs.a: Kearns is a city. It incorporated on May 1, 2024, after serving as a township and then a metro township. Many services still come through the Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District.

faqs.q: Who handles building permits in Kearns?
faqs.a: The Greater Salt Lake Municipal Services District handles building permits, business licensing, land use, zoning, code enforcement and stormwater. Its main number is 385-910-5600.

faqs.q: What is the property tax deadline in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: November 30. Taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the appeal window runs from July 31 to September 15.

faqs.q: Does Kearns have its own police and fire department?
faqs.a: No. Police and fire service come from Unified Police and Unified Fire.

faqs.q: How many people live in Kearns?
faqs.a: The 2020 count was 36,723, and the estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,404.
